_meta.purpose: Manual evaluation fixture for the Milestone 3 AI conversation-extraction contract (src/lib/ai/schema.ts). Used to sanity-check extraction quality by eye during the assessment interview -- it is NOT a unit test fixture (see tests/ai-*.test.ts for those, which use a fake provider and never call a real model).
_meta.labelProvenance: All `expected` fields below are MANUALLY CURATED by a human reading each transcript, not generated by any model and not silently invented. They are a reference for judging whether a real provider run is reasonable, not a strict pass/fail oracle -- see 'numericInterpretationDisclaimer'.
_meta.numericInterpretationDisclaimer: Colombian colloquial amounts (e.g. '1 palos', '2,0 millones', '1000mil') are inherently a little ambiguous even for a human reader. The numeric `budget`/`downPayment` values below are the curator's best-effort interpretation, provided as a reference point -- a reasonable extraction that parses the same phrase slightly differently (e.g. rounding) should not automatically be scored as wrong.
_meta.datasetSource: 16 of the 18 cases are copied verbatim (conversation id, lead id, messages) from data/raw/conversaciones.json, part of the ~677 conversations shipped with the assessment.
_meta.syntheticCasesDisclosure: 2 of the 18 cases (id starting with SYNTH-) are NOT from the supplied dataset. They were constructed by hand, quoting verbatim the two worked examples given in the Milestone 3 task spec itself (customer-priority override, and the ambiguous 'Bajaj Pulsar' motorcycle family) -- see each case's `syntheticNote`. They exist because neither pattern occurs naturally in the 677 supplied conversations: every advisor message in the dataset only ever proposes sending a quote (never an appointment), every customer who is offered a quote accepts it, and every customer who names a 'Pulsar' always includes NS or RS (grep-verified, no bare-family mention exists in data/raw/conversaciones.json). This is disclosed rather than silently presented as real customer data.

messages.texto: Buenas, quiero información de la Bajaj Pulsar NS 160
¡Buenas tardes! Con mucho gusto le colaboro. La Bajaj Pulsar NS 160 está en $11.290.000 más matrícula y SOAT. ¿La está buscando de contado o financiada?
¿Y no tienen algo más económico? tipo la Honda CB 190R
Claro. la Honda CB 190R está en $13.990.000 más papeles
Esa sí me sirve. Tengo 1000mil de inicial
¿Mañana los visito?

motorcycleInterest: ¿Y no tienen algo más económico? tipo la Honda CB 190R

cases.rationale: Deliberately tricky: the lead opened asking about the Pulsar NS 160, but the customer pivots mid-conversation to a DIFFERENT brand's model (Honda CB 190R) and that is what they actually commit to and ask to visit for. Extraction must track the customer's final stated interest, not the conversation's opening topic. paymentMethod is inferred as CREDIT only because 'inicial' (down payment) is a financing-only concept -- never restated explicitly as 'financiada' here, so a lower confidence is appropriate.

messages.texto: Buen día, vi el anuncio de la AKT TTR 200
¡Buenos días! Con mucho gusto le colaboro. La AKT TTR 200 está en $9.890.000 más matrícula y SOAT. ¿La está buscando de contado o financiada?
¿Sigue interesado? quedo atento

motorcycleInterest: vi el anuncio de la AKT TTR 200

cases.rationale: The customer never responds after the advisor's price question -- there is exactly one customer message in the whole conversation. Every commercial field beyond the stated model must be UNKNOWN/null; nothing here supports guessing intent, payment method, or an objection. Also a real ORPHAN-adjacent edge case for the AI stage: still eligible (has a resolvable leadId) but thin on content.

motorcycleInterest: quiero información de la Honda Navi
downPayment: Tengo como 1 palos, ¿alcanza para la inicial?

cases.syntheticNote: Quotes verbatim the worked example from the Milestone 3 task spec, section 'CUSTOMER MESSAGE PRIORITY'. Not present in data/raw/conversaciones.json -- see _meta.syntheticCasesDisclosure.

messages.texto: Te puedo agendar una cita.
No gracias, solo estoy mirando.

cases.rationale: The advisor PROPOSES an appointment, but the customer explicitly declines it. requestedAppointment MUST be false (the advisor's offer is not customer intent), and purchaseIntent must reflect the customer's own 'solo estoy mirando' (LOW), not the advisor's proactive offer. This is the exact failure mode the spec warns against: an extractor that treats advisor claims as customer intent would wrongly set requestedAppointment=true here.

cases.syntheticNote: Quotes verbatim the worked example from the Milestone 3 task spec, section 'MOTORCYCLE RESOLUTION' ('Bajaj Pulsar' -> ambiguous across 3 catalog SKUs). Not present in data/raw/conversaciones.json -- grep-verified that no conversation in the supplied dataset ever mentions a bare 'Pulsar' without NS/RS. See _meta.syntheticCasesDisclosure.

messages.texto: Hola, me interesa la Bajaj Pulsar
¡Claro! Tenemos varias versiones de la Pulsar, ¿cuál le interesa: la NS 125, la NS 160 o la RS 200?
No sé, cualquiera que sea económica

postExtractionResolution.note: The AI must extract the free text exactly as said ('Bajaj Pulsar'), NEVER inventing a specific SKU/trim on its own even though the advisor lists the three options. The deterministic catalog matcher (src/lib/normalization/motorcycle.ts) then runs on that text and correctly leaves it unresolved -- 'pulsar' alone ties across SKU-008/SKU-009/SKU-010 at the same token-similarity score, all below the 0.6 threshold, matching the exact behavior already covered in tests/build-lead-record.test.ts.

cases.rationale: Demonstrates spec item 10 end-to-end: LLM extracts the ambiguous free text faithfully instead of guessing a trim; the separate deterministic matcher (not the LLM) is responsible for resolution and correctly stays unresolved rather than force-matching.
